text:
Casey Mittelstadt is doing a third-line job well. He has 5 goals and 9 points in 17 games in 14:13 a night, and Boston takes 55 percent of the expected goals with him on the ice at 5v5, three points better than without him. He scored against Chicago on Oct. 31 in the Bruins' comeback win.

Some of the scoring is borrowed. He is shooting 20.8 percent, and Boston has scored 7.05 more goals than its chances with him on the ice, which is a lot for a depth center. Expect fewer of them to go in.

What should hold is the passing. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 81st percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.4 wins, mostly from even-strength offense. The eighth overall pick in 2017 never became the top-line center Buffalo hoped for, but a center who wins his minutes on a third line is worth plenty. Our range has him around 45 points.
headline: Mittelstadt fits in as Boston's third-line playmaker
